key_insight: A two-stage data-driven workflow can accurately model molecule–perovskite surface passivation by combining broad perovskite training data with a small, task-specific fine-tuning set.
engineering_relevance: This enables more realistic simulation of defect-passivating molecules on hybrid halide perovskite surfaces, supporting rational design of more stable and higher-performance solar-cell interfaces.
method: Built a large open benchmark dataset of diverse metal and hybrid halide perovskite structures (hyP-26).
Added a small specialized dataset for an amino-silane passivating molecule to fine-tune the model.
Used a multistep training pipeline similar to continuous fine-tuning to study surface coverage effects at a mixed-composition perovskite surface.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a curated open dataset plus a specialized fine-tuning dataset and shows the approach can probe how interactions evolve as amino-silane coverage increases.
watch_item: Performance may depend strongly on the quality and representativeness of the small specialized fine-tuning dataset, especially for experimentally realistic surface chemistries.
paper_title: Data-driven atomistic modelling of hybrid halide perovskite passivation
